Visualize a compositional variable

Source: R/plot_compD.R
plot.compD.Rd

Draws per-part density curves and boxplots of the untransformed parts of a declare_composition() object, the ternary plots of the composition and the heatmap of its variation matrix, all from the object's imputed composition. When the object carries flagged compositional outliers (declare_composition()'s detect_outliers), two further panels show the outlier distances and the flagged observations in the simplex.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'compD'
plot(
  x,
  histogram = TRUE,
  boxplot = TRUE,
  ternary = TRUE,
  variation = TRUE,
  outliers = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A compD object from declare_composition().

histogram

Logical; include per-part density curves (ggplot2::geom_density(), faceted by part). Default TRUE.

boxplot

Logical; include per-part boxplots (ggplot2::geom_boxplot()). Default TRUE.

ternary

Logical; include the ternary plot(s) (plot_ternary()). Default TRUE. Set FALSE for a two-part composition, which has no ternary representation; this also drops the outlier ternary.

variation

Logical; include the variation-matrix heatmap (plot_variation()). Default TRUE.

outliers

Logical; include the outlier panels. Default TRUE. The panels appear only when x carries flagged outliers, so a composition declared without detect_outliers is unaffected.

...

Further arguments passed to plot_ternary() (e.g., group). They do not reach the outlier panels, which always describe the whole sample (see Value).

Value

Invisibly, a named list of the requested plots, with elements histogram, boxplot, ternary (a single ggtern plot or, for more than three parts, a named list of choose(D, 3) panels) and variation (the variation-matrix heatmap). When x carries flagged outliers, two further elements follow: outliers, the Mahalanobis distance of each observation against the cutoff, and, unless ternary = FALSE, outlier_ternary, the ternary panel(s) with the flagged observations highlighted. Both describe the whole sample and are never split by group. Calling plot() draws the plots as a side effect.

See also

declare_composition() to build the compD object; summary.compD() for the descriptive tables; plot_ternary() and plot_variation() for the ternary and variation-matrix figures alone.

Other declare and describe composition: comp_impute(), comp_outliers(), declare_composition(), summary.compD()

Examples

# \donttest{
cd <- declare_composition(timeuse, c("MVPA", "LPA", "SB", "SPT"),
                          closure = 1440)
plots <- plot(cd)







plots$boxplot

# }
